title: 한눈에 ③: 먼저? 바로? 그동안? 시간·순서 연결 구별하기
objective: By the end, you can choose the right ending to say "after," "as soon as," "while," or "stopped A and did B," and avoid the common tense and subject mistakes with these endings.
summary: A one-page overview of six Korean endings that link two actions in time: -고서, -고 나서, -자마자, -는 사이에, -는 대로, and -다가.

task.title: Choose, fix, and connect
task.line: Use the table on page 1 to pick, correct, or write the ending that shows the right time order.

forms.when: Action verbs. Both actions have the same subject. Do not add past tense before -고서.
forms.means: did A, and then B (A leads straight into B)
forms.exampleMeaning: My friend heard what I said and then laughed.

forms.when: Action verbs. A is completely finished before B starts. Usually the same subject. No past tense before -고 나서.
forms.exampleMeaning: I play games after I finish all my homework.

forms.when: Action verbs. B happens right after A. The subject can change. Works for past, present, and future.
forms.exampleMeaning: It started raining as soon as I got off the bus.

forms.when: Action verbs. B happens during A, often while no one notices. The two parts usually have different subjects.
forms.means: while A is going on, B happens
forms.exampleMeaning: I did the laundry while the baby was sleeping.

forms.when: Action verbs. Use it for plans, promises, and requests (future, -(으)세요, -(으)ㄹ게요). Not for past events.
forms.means: as soon as A (happens), I will / please do B
forms.exampleMeaning: I'll contact you as soon as the results come out.

forms.when: Action verbs. You stop doing A, or something happens in the middle of A, and B follows. Both parts have the same subject.
forms.means: while doing A, (switched to / ran into) B
forms.exampleMeaning: I ran into a friend while I was walking down the street.

watchOut: 먹었고 나서 (X) → 먹고 나서 (O): Never put past tense before -고 나서, -고서, or -자마자. Show the tense at the end of the sentence.
도착하는 대로 전화했어요 (X) → 도착하자마자 전화했어요 (O): -는 대로 is for plans and requests. For things that already happened, use -자마자.
제가 자다가 동생이 TV를 켰어요 (X) → 제가 자는 사이에 동생이 TV를 켰어요 (O): -다가 needs the same subject. If someone else does B, use -는 사이에.
제가 전화를 받고서 친구가 나갔어요 (X) → 제가 전화를 받자마자 친구가 나갔어요 (O): -고서 needs the same subject. If the subject changes, use -자마자.
exercises: Choose the right form: ① 수업이 (끝나자마자 / 끝나는 사이에) 학생들이 교실 밖으로 나갔어요. ② 제가 잠깐 (졸다가 / 조는 사이에) 지하철이 우리 역을 지나갔어요.
Fill in the blanks with 보다 + -는 사이에 or -다가: ① 엄마가 장을 ____ 아빠는 청소를 했어요. ② 저는 TV를 ____ 잠이 들었어요.
Choose the right form: ① 서류를 (받는 대로 / 받았는 대로) 바로 보내 주세요. ② 어제는 집에 (오는 대로 / 오자마자) 샤워했어요.
Find and fix the mistake: ① 운동했고 나서 샤워했어요. ② 회의가 끝났자마자 퇴근했어요.
Join the two sentences with the ending given: ① 이를 닦았어요. 잤어요. (-고 나서) ② 그 사람은 전화를 받았어요. 아무 말 없이 나갔어요. (-고서)
Answer in Korean using -는 대로: 언제 출발할 거예요? (일이 끝나다)
answers: ① 운동하고 나서 샤워했어요. ② 회의가 끝나자마자 퇴근했어요.
① 이를 닦고 나서 잤어요. ② 그 사람은 전화를 받고서 아무 말 없이 나갔어요.
일이 끝나는 대로 출발할 거예요. (일이 끝나는 대로 출발해요.)
